posts.title: Pale Flower (1964)
posts.description: I watched Pale Flower 乾いた花 almost by accident. It had been sitting on a study list when I was watching Japanese films, and one day I noticed it was only about ninety minutes long. The title sounded nice. Two minutes into the film, the protagonist, Muraki, tells you immediately what kind of man he is. He just got out of prison and makes his way back to Tokyo. posts.title: Water Bellies
posts.description: It rained. Finally. I often check the forecast, maybe daily, hoping to see icons of clouds, droplets, or thunder. It had been a very dry summer where I live. The heat wasn’t as bad as it was two years ago, it was fine, but the season felt lifeless and boring without water pouring down through muggy air, without thunder growling in distant clouds. posts.title: On Story and Design Choices in Modern Games
posts.description: I had been writing down game ideas for a while. Lots of text, cool art, interesting mechanics. Excellent. Very useful. The ideas usually worked until they did not. At some point the parts began to feel attached to one another instead of necessary, and I kept wondering how other games avoided that.
